base.$description:
The default stacking level: content in the normal flow of the page. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Page content, and anything that does not need to sit above its neighbours. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not set it to push an element up — that is z-index.raised.

raised.$description:
An element lifted just above its neighbours in the same flow. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
A hovered or selected card that must overlap its siblings, a badge over an avatar. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for anything that leaves the flow — a menu opening is z-index.dropdown, a pinned bar z-index.sticky. Do not set it just because a card carries elevation.raised — that is the shadow, not the stacking; use it only when the element must overlap a sibling.

dropdown.$description:
The level of a panel that opens from a control and overlaps the content below it. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Dropdown panel, select or combobox list, date picker opened from a field. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for a panel that must cover a modal — that is z-index.popover.

sticky.$description:
The level of an element that sticks to an edge while the content scrolls under it. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Sticky header, sticky table header, a toolbar that sticks while scrolling. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for an element fixed to the viewport regardless of scroll — that is z-index.fixed.

fixed.$description:
The level of an element fixed to the viewport. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
A fixed app bar, a bottom navigation bar, a floating action button. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for the scrim behind a modal — that is z-index.overlay.

overlay.$description:
The level of the scrim that dims the page behind a modal surface. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
The color-surface.static.overlay layer behind a modal, drawer or bottom sheet. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not put the modal itself here — that is z-index.modal, one level above its scrim.

modal.$description:
The level of a modal surface, above its scrim. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Modal, dialog, drawer and bottom sheet. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for a menu or popover opened from inside a modal — that is z-index.popover.

popover.$description:
The level of a floating panel that must open above a modal. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Popover, menu or dropdown opened from inside a modal or drawer. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for a dropdown on the page — that is z-index.dropdown.

toast.$description:
The level of a transient notification above everything the user is working in. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Toast and snackbar. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for a tooltip, which sits even higher — that is z-index.tooltip.

tooltip.$description:
The highest stacking level: short help attached to the pointer or focus. Same in every brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
Tooltip. Only in code: no Figma property takes a stacking order.

Do not:
Do not use it for anything that holds interactive content — a panel with actions is z-index.popover.
